title: 3 John Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 3 John chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 3 John Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 3 John Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 3 John 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The elder's wish for health and prosperity
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:1 begins with the elder's greeting to the wellbeloved Gaius, which is the first event mentioned.

questions.question: To whom is the elder writing in 3 John 1?
questions.explanation: The elder addresses the letter specifically to Gaius, as stated in 3 John 1:1.

questions.question: How does the elder describe his love for Gaius in 3 John 1:1?
questions.explanation: The elder says he loves Gaius 'in the truth' in 3 John 1:1.

questions.question: What does the elder wish for Gaius above all things according to 3 John 1:2?
options: That he may prosper and be in health
That he may preach the truth
questions.correctAnswer: That he may prosper and be in health
questions.explanation: In 3 John 1:2, the elder expresses a wish that Gaius may prosper and be in health.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:2, what is the condition related to the elder's wish for Gaius's prosperity and health?
questions.explanation: The elder wishes that Gaius may prosper and be in health 'even as thy soul prospereth' as stated in 3 John 1:2.

questions.question: What cause of joy does the elder mention in 3 John 1:3?
options: Brethren testified of the truth in Gaius
questions.correctAnswer: Brethren testified of the truth in Gaius
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:3 states that the elder rejoiced greatly when brethren testified of the truth in Gaius.

questions.question: How does the elder describe Gaius's walk according to 3 John 1:3?
questions.explanation: The elder notes that Gaius walks in the truth in 3 John 1:3.

questions.question: What is the elder's greatest joy as expressed in 3 John 1:4?
options: Hearing that his children walk in truth
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing that his children walk in truth
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:4 states the elder has no greater joy than hearing that his children walk in truth.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:5, how does the elder describe Gaius's actions toward the brethren and strangers?
questions.explanation: The elder calls Gaius faithful in all he does toward brethren and strangers in 3 John 1:5.

questions.question: Who does Gaius do faithfully what he does to, according to 3 John 1:5?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:5 states that Gaius faithfully does whatever he does to both brethren and strangers.

questions.question: What does the elder call Gaius in 3 John 1:1?
questions.explanation: The elder refers to Gaius as the 'wellbeloved' in 3 John 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: The elder expresses joy when hearing that his children walk in truth.
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:4 explicitly states the elder has no greater joy than hearing that his children walk in truth.

questions.question: True or False: The elder wishes that Gaius may prosper and be in health as his soul prospers.
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:2 expresses the elder's wish that Gaius may prosper and be in health even as his soul prospers.

questions.question: True or False: The elder says that Gaius is joyful and generous toward strangers.
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:5 states that Gaius does things faithfully toward brethren and strangers; the terms 'joyful' and 'generous' are not used.

questions.question: True or False: The elder writes to Gaius telling him to love the brethren.
questions.explanation: The text does not contain a command telling Gaius to love the brethren; it states the elder loves Gaius and commends his faithfulness.

medium.title: 3 John Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 3 John Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:6, what should you do if you bring forward those who have borne witness of your charity on their journey?
options: Bring them forward after a godly sort
questions.correctAnswer: Bring them forward after a godly sort
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:6 commands that if you bring forward those who have borne witness of your charity, you should do so after a godly sort.

questions.question: What does 3 John 1:8 promise will happen if we receive such brethren as mentioned in 3 John 1:7?
options: We might be fellowhelpers to the truth
We will be praised by the church
questions.correctAnswer: We might be fellowhelpers to the truth
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:8 promises that if we receive such brethren (those who went forth for Christ's name, taking nothing of the Gentiles), we might be fellowhelpers to the truth.

questions.question: Why did the brethren go forth according to 3 John 1:7?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:7 states that the brethren went forth for his name's sake, meaning for the sake of Christ's name.

questions.question: What behavior of Diotrephes is described in 3 John 1:9 and 3 John 1:10?
options: He loves preeminence and refuses to receive the brethren
He welcomes all with open arms
He preaches humbly and supports the elder
He sends aid to the brethren
questions.correctAnswer: He loves preeminence and refuses to receive the brethren
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:9-10 describe Diotrephes as loving to have the preeminence and not receiving the elder or brethren, and even casting some out of the church.

questions.question: How does the elder describe his joy in 3 John 1:4 in relation to the behavior of the brethren?
options: He has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth
He is indifferent to their conduct
He is disappointed when they do well
He desires only material success for them
questions.correctAnswer: He has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:4 states that the elder has no greater joy than hearing that his children walk in truth, showing the importance of living in truth.

questions.question: What action did the elder take toward the church regarding Diotrephes according to 3 John 1:9?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:9 states that the elder wrote unto the church about Diotrephes who was not receiving them.

questions.question: What does Diotrephes do besides not receiving the brethren, as described in 3 John 1:10?
options: He forbids those who want to receive them and casts them out of the church
questions.correctAnswer: He forbids those who want to receive them and casts them out of the church
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:10 states that Diotrephes not only refuses to receive the brethren but also forbids those who would and casts them out of the church.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:5, what is Gaius doing faithfully?
options: Whatsoever he does to the brethren and to strangers
questions.correctAnswer: Whatsoever he does to the brethren and to strangers
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:5 praises Gaius for doing faithfully whatsoever he does to the brethren and to strangers.

questions.question: How does the elder describe his feelings when the brethren testify of the truth in Gaius in 3 John 1:3?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:3 states that the elder rejoiced greatly when the brethren testified of the truth that is in Gaius.

questions.question: What is the elder's wish for Gaius expressed in 3 John 1:2?
options: That he may prosper and be in health, even as his soul prospereth
That he may gain riches quickly
That he may be free from persecution
questions.correctAnswer: That he may prosper and be in health, even as his soul prospereth
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:2 expresses the elder's wish that Gaius may prosper and be in health, even as his soul prospereth.

questions.question: What is the reason the brethren took nothing from the Gentiles according to 3 John 1:7?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:7 states that the brethren took nothing of the Gentiles for his name's sake, indicating their mission was sincere and not for material gain.

questions.question: What practical Christian living principle can be drawn from 3 John 1:8 about receiving brethren?
options: Receiving such brethren makes us fellowhelpers to the truth
We should be cautious and suspicious of strangers
We must always test brethren before helping
It is better to help only those we know well
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving such brethren makes us fellowhelpers to the truth
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:8 teaches that receiving brethren who go forth for Christ's name makes us fellowhelpers to the truth, emphasizing hospitality and cooperation in Christian living.

questions.question: What is the elder's attitude toward Diotrephes' prating against them with malicious words as per 3 John 1:10?
options: He will remember his deeds if he comes
He joins in the malicious words
questions.correctAnswer: He will remember his deeds if he comes
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:10 states that if the elder comes, he will remember Diotrephes' deeds which include malicious words and refusal to receive the brethren.

questions.question: True or False: According to 3 John 1:1, the elder writes to Gaius whom he loves in the truth.
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:1 states the elder writes to the wellbeloved Gaius, whom he loves in the truth.

questions.question: True or False: According to 3 John 1:6, it is acceptable to bring forward brethren on their journey without regard to godly conduct.
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:6 specifies bringing forward brethren on their journey after a godly sort, indicating the importance of godly conduct.

hard.title: 3 John Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 3 John Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:11, what should we follow?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:11 states, 'Beloved, follow not that which is evil, but that which is good.' This indicates that we should pursue goodness over evil.

questions.question: Who is mentioned in 3 John 1:12 as having a good report?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:12 specifically states, 'Demetrius hath good report of all men, and of the truth itself,' highlighting his positive reputation.

questions.question: What does 3 John 1:13 indicate about the author's writing?
options: He is writing out of obligation
He had many things to write but chose not to
He wrote for the sake of writing
questions.correctAnswer: He had many things to write but chose not to
questions.explanation: In 3 John 1:13, the author states, 'I had many things to write, but I will not with ink and pen write unto thee,' implying a selective approach to communication.

questions.question: What does 3 John 1:14 express regarding the author's future plans?
options: He hopes to see Gaius shortly
He is uncertain about his journey
questions.correctAnswer: He hopes to see Gaius shortly
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:14 says, 'But I trust I shall shortly see thee,' indicating the author's desire and expectation to meet Gaius soon.

questions.question: According to 3 John 1:11, what is the relationship between doing good and knowing God?
options: He that doeth good is of God
questions.correctAnswer: He that doeth good is of God
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:11 states that 'He that doeth good is of God,' establishing a direct correlation between good actions and a relationship with God.

questions.question: In 3 John 1:10, what negative behavior does Diotrephes exhibit?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:10 mentions that Diotrephes 'prating against us with malicious words,' indicating his negative behavior towards the author.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'agathos' in 3 John 1:11 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Agathos' means 'good' in Greek, aligning with the instruction in 3 John 1:11 to follow what is good.

questions.question: What literary device is used in 3 John 1:11 with the phrases 'that which is evil' and 'that which is good'?
questions.explanation: The contrasting phrases 'that which is evil' and 'that which is good' in 3 John 1:11 demonstrate antithesis, highlighting opposition.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of truth as seen in 3 John 1:3?
questions.explanation: John 8:32 states, 'And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free,' connecting to the theme of truth in 3 John 1:3.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage emphasizes doing good as seen in 3 John 1:11?
questions.explanation: Galatians 6:9 encourages believers to 'not be weary in well doing,' which echoes the call to do good in 3 John 1:11.

questions.question: What comes before 3 John 1:11?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:11 follows directly after 3 John 1:10, which discusses Diotrephes' negative actions.

questions.question: What comes after 3 John 1:12?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:12 is followed by 3 John 1:13, where the author discusses not writing everything down.

questions.question: The good report of Demetrius is highlighted in the context of what theme?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:12 emphasizes Demetrius' good report 'of the truth itself,' connecting him to the theme of truth.

questions.question: It is true that 3 John emphasizes the importance of community and support among believers.
questions.explanation: 3 John emphasizes community support, as seen in verses discussing hospitality and receiving brethren.

questions.question: It is false that 3 John categorically condemns all forms of leadership within the church.
questions.explanation: 3 John critiques Diotrephes for his behavior, but it does not condemn all leadership, rather it advocates for good leadership.

theological.title: 3 John Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 3 John Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 3 John 1:2 teach about sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves prosperity and health aligned with the soul's wellbeing
Sanctification is solely about moral behavior without regard to physical condition
Sanctification excludes any concern for earthly prosperity
Sanctification is only a future hope and not linked to present conditions
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves prosperity and health aligned with the soul's wellbeing
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:2 expresses a wish for prosperity and health 'even as thy soul prospereth,' linking physical and spiritual wellbeing, which supports a holistic view of sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine does 3 John 1:7 teach about the nature of Christian mission?
options: Christian mission is carried out sacrificially for the sake of Christ's name without seeking worldly support
Christian mission requires financial support from Gentiles for legitimacy
Christian mission is primarily about cultural assimilation
Christian mission focuses on personal gain and recognition
questions.correctAnswer: Christian mission is carried out sacrificially for the sake of Christ's name without seeking worldly support
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:7 states that they 'went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles,' emphasizing sacrificial mission for Christ's name without reliance on worldly resources.

questions.question: What doctrine does 3 John 1:11 teach about human sin and divine knowledge?
options: Doing evil indicates a lack of true knowledge of God
Human sin is unrelated to knowledge of God
Evil deeds are always known and accepted by God
Sin is only external and does not affect divine relationship
questions.correctAnswer: Doing evil indicates a lack of true knowledge of God
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:11 contrasts good and evil deeds, stating that 'he that doeth evil hath not seen God,' teaching a doctrinal link between sin and spiritual blindness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 3 John 1:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:4 reveals the elder's joy when hearing that 'my children walk in truth,' demonstrating God's attribute of delight or joyfulness in the faithfulness of His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 3 John 1:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:8 encourages receiving those who labor for the truth so we might be 'fellowhelpers to the truth,' reflecting God's covenant faithfulness in sustaining His truth through His people.

questions.question: How does 3 John 1:9 connect to the broader New Testament teaching on church leadership and authority?
options: It warns against pride and authoritarianism in church leaders
It endorses absolute hierarchical control without accountability
It teaches that church leaders should be isolated from other believers
It promotes disobedience to apostolic authority
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against pride and authoritarianism in church leaders
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:9 criticizes Diotrephes for loving preeminence and rejecting apostolic authority, aligning with New Testament warnings against prideful leadership (cf. 1 Timothy 3).

questions.question: How does 3 John 1:6 prepare for the New Testament theme of hospitality as a Christian virtue?
options: It presents hospitality to traveling brethren as a godly practice commended by the church
It limits hospitality only to family members
It teaches that hospitality is optional and insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: It presents hospitality to traveling brethren as a godly practice commended by the church
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:6 emphasizes hospitality to brethren and strangers as a testimony to charity, reinforcing hospitality as essential in Christian conduct (cf. Hebrews 13:2).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 John 1:5 and 3 John 1:6 teach about Christian service and charity?
options: Faithful service to both brethren and strangers is a demonstration of genuine charity acknowledged by the church
Service should be limited to only those within one's local community
Charity is primarily about financial giving, not hospitality
Christian charity is an optional act not linked to faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful service to both brethren and strangers is a demonstration of genuine charity acknowledged by the church
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 commend faithful deeds toward brethren and strangers, showing charity witnessed and honored by the church, emphasizing broad Christian service.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 John 1:9 and 3 John 1:10 teach about church discipline and false leadership?
options: Church discipline must oppose prideful leaders who reject apostolic authority and exclude brethren
Church leaders should exercise unchecked power without accountability
False leadership is tolerated to avoid conflict
Church discipline is unnecessary in cases of schism
questions.correctAnswer: Church discipline must oppose prideful leaders who reject apostolic authority and exclude brethren
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:9-10 criticizes Diotrephes for rejecting apostolic messengers and casting out brethren, teaching the necessity of opposing such prideful leadership through discipline.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 John 1:12 and 3 John 1:3 teach about Christian testimony and truth?
options: A good report and faithful walking in truth mutually affirm the authenticity of Christian testimony
Testimony is irrelevant to Christian fellowship
Truth is subjective and varies by community report
Christian testimony is primarily about miracles
questions.correctAnswer: A good report and faithful walking in truth mutually affirm the authenticity of Christian testimony
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:3 rejoices in the brethren's testimony of truth in Gaius, while 1:12 affirms Demetrius’s good report, combining to teach the doctrinal value of consistent faithful testimony.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 3 John 1:9-10 endorses authoritarianism in church leadership by supporting Diotrephes’ actions. What does 3 John 1:9-10 actually teach?
options: The passage condemns Diotrephes’ authoritarianism and refusal to receive the apostolic messengers
It supports Diotrephes’ exclusive control over the church
It suggests that rejecting brethren is commendable
It portrays Diotrephes as a model leader
questions.correctAnswer: The passage condemns Diotrephes’ authoritarianism and refusal to receive the apostolic messengers
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:9-10 explicitly states that Diotrephes 'receiveth us not,' 'prating against us,' and 'casteth them out,' showing condemnation rather than endorsement of authoritarianism.

questions.question: What doctrine does 3 John 1:1 teach about the nature of Christian love?
options: Christian love is grounded in truth and is not merely emotional
Christian love is unconditional without reference to truth
Christian love is primarily social convenience
questions.correctAnswer: Christian love is grounded in truth and is not merely emotional
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:1 states the elder loves Gaius 'in the truth,' showing that Christian love is rooted in doctrinal truth, not mere sentiment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 3 John 1:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:14 concludes with a blessing of peace to Gaius, reflecting God's attribute as the giver of peace to His people.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 John 1:11 and 3 John 1:5 teach about moral discernment and obedience within the church?
options: Believers are called to reject evil and practice good as evidence of knowing God and faithful service
Moral choices are irrelevant to Christian identity
Obedience to church leaders is more important than moral goodness
Doing evil is permissible if it benefits the church
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to reject evil and practice good as evidence of knowing God and faithful service
questions.explanation: Verse 11 calls to 'follow not that which is evil, but that which is good,' and verse 5 commends faithful deeds to brethren and strangers, combining to teach moral obedience as proof of divine knowledge.

questions.question: How does 3 John 1:13-14 contribute to the broader narrative arc of apostolic authority and fellowship in the early church?
options: It anticipates personal fellowship and peace among believers as a sign of apostolic unity and authority
It denies the importance of personal visits among believers
It suggests that written communication is superior to face-to-face fellowship
It advocates isolation from the church community
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates personal fellowship and peace among believers as a sign of apostolic unity and authority
questions.explanation: 3 John 1:13-14 expresses the elder's desire to meet face to face and extend peace, highlighting the importance of personal fellowship in apostolic ministry.
